title: Fit both beaters into a hand mixer, the right one in each socket
keywords: find the slot angle by turning
instruction: Fit both beaters into the hand mixer so that each is fully in and locked, then let go of everything. The mixer must stay standing on its heel rest on the table.
context: Fitting the beaters is an everyday home-baking step: people do it every time they use a hand mixer at home to whip cream, beat eggs or mix cake batter. Hand mixers sell by the million: KitchenAid's one plant that makes all its hand mixers built 1 million of them in 2016, and the brand makes more than 2 million stand mixers a year there (Daily Advocate, 'Million mixer milestone', 16 Nov 2016, dailyadvocate.com, opened 2026-11-19). 43% of US consumers own a stand mixer (AHAM consumer research, blog.aham.org, 13 Aug 2018, opened 2026-11-19). The maker's help page (producthelp.kitchenaid.com, 'Inserting the Beaters - Hand Mixer', opened 2026-11-19) gives the steps: the beater with the collar goes in the larger opening, turn the flanges to the slots, push to lock, then the other beater in the smaller opening. The skill: the two beaters look alike, but the collared one fits only the larger socket, so the plain one must go in the smaller one; the slot angle is not known and is found by turning the beater under a light push; and the free-standing mixer moves under the locking push unless the other hand braces it. How this differs from fitting a stand mixer's beater: that is one beater on one shaft, slid up until its bayonet pocket meets the shaft's pin and then turned to lock, on a heavy base that does not move; no choice of socket, no hidden slot angle and no brace. It also differs from swapping a hand blender's attachment: one attachment pushed or twisted onto one coupling while the other hand holds the blender's body in the air. Here there are two near-identical parts and two sockets that only one order fills, a blind slot search under a light push, and a free-standing body that one hand must brace on the table while the other pushes.
setup: Positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. (1) Hand mixer, KitchenAid 5-speed hand mixer class (e.g. KHM512), white ABS housing, 0.9 kg, standing upright on its rubber heel rest. Housing 70 x 90 x 190 mm above a 125 x 80 x 10 mm heel rest; handle loop behind the housing: a 25 x 25 mm bar 135 mm tall joined by two 30 mm struts. The underside (socket face) faces the robot's right arm (-y), the handle faces the left arm. Two sockets 38 mm apart, centres 65 mm above the table: the larger opening 14.5 mm square, the smaller 11.8 mm square, in a 4 mm face plate. Inside each: a brass drive spindle (13 mm across, four 3 mm slots, from 4 to 19 mm deep) geared to the motor so it holds its angle; then a 7.2 mm bore to 38 mm deep with a spring clip (4 mm steel ball at 30 mm depth, sprung into the bore). Start: footprint centre at x 300 mm, y +20 mm, each trial moved up to +/-30 mm in x and y and turned up to +/-20 deg; each spindle at a random angle (0-90 deg). (2) Collared beater, stainless steel wire beater, 60 g, 190 mm long: 6 mm stem, 13 mm collar 32-36 mm from the tip, four fins 10 mm across, 2 mm thick, 24-32 mm from the tip (between collar and tip), a 4 mm wide groove 4.5-8.5 mm from the rounded tip; cage of four wire blades 40 mm across and 70 mm long. (3) Plain beater: the same with a 10 mm shoulder in place of the collar, 55 g. Both lie flat on two blades in front of the mixer, stems pointing +y toward the socket face, tips at y -65 mm (+/-12 mm), one at x 185 mm, the other at x 115 mm (+/-8 mm), each turned up to +/-12 deg; which beater lies in which place is random. The screenshot shows seed 0. Real trial: the seed's layout is drawn on paper under the table's clear mat; spindle angles are set by hand to the README's list (paint dot on each spindle).
scoring: Scored at the end of the run. Per beater (0.4 each): 0.1 if its stem is in a socket (tip at least 6 mm past the socket face, on the socket axis within 1.5 mm and 6 deg); +0.1 if the fins are in the slots (tip at least 30 mm deep; with the fins off the slots the tip stops at 28 mm); +0.2 if clipped (tip within 1.5 mm of full depth, 36 mm, and the clip ball back in the groove). The collared beater counts only in the larger socket; the plain one in either (the maker: a beater without a collar fits either opening). +0.2 if the mixer stands on its heel rest (tilt at most 5 deg) with its footprint centre within 5 mm of where it started (braced demos moved it 0.4 to 1.8 mm; with no brace the locking pushes slid it 11.6 mm on seed 0). The trial scores 0 unless both grippers end at least 20 mm from the mixer and both beaters. Real trial: a ruler from the socket face to the top of the blade cage (fully in: 84 mm exposed; fins in: 90 mm or less; in the socket: 114 mm or less); clipped = it stays in when the mixer is lifted 10 cm by its handle and held 3 s; tape measure from the marked start; a photo of both grippers clear.
reset_notes: Press the mixer's ejector (in the real trial) or pull each beater straight out, lay both beaters flat beside the mixer as the seed's layout gives, and turn each drive spindle to the seed's angle by hand (paint dot on the spindle, angle from the list in the README).
fidelity: Rigid PhysX bodies at real size and mass (estimated for a KitchenAid-class mixer; to be measured on a bought unit). All by contact, joints and springs: openings, collar, fins, slots and groove are collision shapes; the spindle's gear train is a hinge spring; the clip is a 4 mm ball on a sprung slider (real: a wire spring clip). Wire blades are straight bars; the two beaters' blades do not collide with each other (real ones mesh). No motor, cord or ejector.
scores: All on one code version, 1,200-step limit. Scripted demo, reads object poses from the simulator: 1.0 on seeds 0, 1 and 2 (872, 872, 884 steps). Fixed plan made for the reference layout, no sensing, seed 0: 0.0 (no beater reaches a socket). Demo with no brace, seed 0: 0.8 (both clipped; the mixer slid 11.6 mm, over the 5 mm limit). Demo with the order swapped, seed 0: 0.6 (plain beater clipped in the larger socket, 0.4; the collared one stops on its collar at 31.9 mm in the smaller socket, 0; mixer held, 0.2). Dream-1, seed 0, 1,200 steps: 0.0 (neither beater reached a socket; both stayed 17 to 19 cm off the socket axes; the mixer did not move).
